chapter: Carnegie Hall and the touring years
title: Atlantic Records and the first rock 'n' roll record
summary: An Atlantic man flew to record him wherever he was; Turner claims the first rock 'n' roll record, 'Shake, Rattle and Roll'.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Then we started playin' universities. I went back to New York, an' my company in New York was bookin' me--Shaw's Booking Agency. So, they started givin' up...puttin' out...I'm gettin' a kinda ahead of myself there now.

So, anyway, I run into the cats had Atlantic Recording Company ...'cause I had...I knew one of the fellows a long time ago...who used to work for Nashville...National...National Records Company. He used to travel all around all...wherever I was he'd come...fellow he was comin' to record me. All I gotta do is call him up, say, "I'm ready to record," an' he would get on a plane an' come. We get us a band and make records.
Who was that? Was that Nesuhi Ertegun?*

Yeah. An' we'd made all kinds of records all over the country. Sometime he come to my house in Chicago an' write... sit down an' write...take my ol' number an' write some other stuff with it an' change the whole thing around.
But anyway, he was travellin' around. So then we got into the business of rock 'n' roll. Were the first record ever was put out in rock 'n' roll, I did it.
What was the name of it?
*[Other sources suggest that this more likely was Ahmet Ertegun, rather than Nesuhi. --P.W.]
